title: Media Inquiry: Channel 10 — will you keep flying near homes?

fields.message: Will the Group keep flying near homes and the airport? What has it changed since this morning?

instructorNote: Watch for the approved measures stated plainly and no technical guesses.

citations.headingPath: ERP › Section 8 › 8.5 Interference, GNSS anomalies and suspected link compromise
citations.quote: Treat as Level 2. Land all aircraft; preserve the GCS state; call the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead before anything is powered down; no further launches at the site that day; the HUOG-ISP incident play

snapshot.title: Incident Closed — Firmware Root Cause Confirmed

fields.text: Attention all personnel. The UAS-02 incident has been officially closed. The root cause was a firmware bug in version 2.4.11a that disabled the failover logic, resulting in an uncommanded climb into Class C airspace. The decision to ground the fleet was correct and necessary. No further flights will resume until firmware version 2.3.2 is fully validated and approved by the FOM and ASO. The After-Action Note (AAN) has been drafted and submitted via HUOG-ERP Section 11.3 to the FOM, ASO, and FSDO. The incident log is now archived.
fields.zones: ALL HANGAR ZONES, INCIDENT COMMAND POST, GCS-01, HUOG-NAS01 ACCESS
fields.voiceDirection: Calm, authoritative male voice, steady pace, no reverb
fields.terminalAmbience: Quiet control room, faint keyboard taps, distant HVAC hum
fields.deliveryNote: Play the audio on all main speakers. Do not explain it. The AAN is now filed.
fields.scenarioTitle: Lost Signal — Link Failure & Class C Incursion

snapshot.instructorNote: This inject finalizes the incident. The IC must now confirm the AAN is filed and the NAS archive is updated. Watch for any attempt to resume flights or bypass the approval process.
